personality_one_liner: A calm, highly functional travel companion built on soft warm neutrals, crisp typography, and cinematic travel imagery.

spacing.rule: Generous vertical breathing room for reading itineraries. Do not cram data.

do's: Use blur on floating tabs over scrolling content.
Use heavy scrim and blur behind Trip titles overlaying cover photos.
Use glassmorphism for floating action buttons.
dont's: Do not blur individual itinerary item cards.
Do not stack blurs over each other.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: List user's trips categorized into Upcoming, Past, and Wishlist.

states.empty: Empty luggage illustration with 'Plan your next escape' message.

screens.layout: Header with 'My Trips'. A custom pill-shaped segmented control for 'Upcoming/Past/Wishlist'. Vertical list of edge-to-edge or large md-margin cards. Each card is a hero image of the destination with gradient scrim and title (e.g., 'Paris Getaway') anchored to the bottom. FAB at bottom right to 'Create Trip'.

screens.name: TripDetail
screens.purpose: Hub screen for a specific trip containing all sub-tabs.

states.loading: Skeleton layout for header and tab content.

screens.layout: Collapsible image header (full bleed) showing trip cover photo. Trip name over a top-to-bottom dark gradient scrim. Below header: A horizontal scrollable strip of tabs (Itinerary [Default], Flights, Transport, Stay, Attractions, Tickets, Budget). Active tab uses 'brandPrimary' indicator. Below tabs: The active tab's content.

screens.name: ItineraryTab
screens.purpose: Auto-generated day-by-day calendar with chronological items.

states.empty: No items added yet. Add flights or stays to build your itinerary.

screens.layout: Top section: horizontal scroll of filter checkboxes (Flights, Stay, Attractions). Main content: Vertical timeline with distinct Day/Date sticky headers. Individual items shown as cards connecting to the timeline, featuring legible typography for times and simple intuitive Phosphor icons.

screens.name: BudgetTab
screens.purpose: Track planned vs actual expenses without spreadsheet anxiety.
screens.layout: Hero card at the top displaying 'Total Planned' vs 'Total Spent' using a clean progress bar or simple ring, avoiding dense grids. Below: Vertical list of category breakdowns (Flights, Stay, etc.) showing cost subtotals.

screens.name: CategoryTabs (Flights, Transport, Stay, Attractions)
screens.purpose: Dedicated lists and forms for specific booking types.

states.empty: Empty state illustration of a boarding pass/ticket with CTA to add item.

screens.layout: Vertical stacked lists of cards. Each card shows key data (e.g., Flight time/duration/layover) in a linear story format. Includes a clear 'Status' badge (Booked, Not Booked, Pay on Arrival). FAB to add a new item.

instructions_to_main_agent: Follow 1 iOS-Native Clean. Maintain generous padding and use Geist for all UI text to ensure high legibility of times/dates.

Implement a hub-and-spoke model for TripDetail: The header stays at the top, a horizontal ScrollView of tabs sits just below it, and the content swaps out based on selection to avoid ping-pong navigation.
All hero images must have a 3-stop vertical gradient scrim (transparent -> 20% dark -> 70% dark) to ensure the white trip names are readable.

For the Itinerary tab, use a vertical timeline. Keep the timeline visual clear and separate the time headers from the card content. Implement a top horizontal scroll for checkboxes allowing users to toggle categories on/off.
Budget should avoid dense grids; rely on a clean hero card for total budget, and simple vertical list for categories.
Data entry forms (e.g. flight layovers, dates) must use native components and clearly structure inputs in a single column layout.
All bookings must include a status selection UI (Booked, Not Booked, Pay on Arrival).
